status: draft; priority and scope await three-party agreement

contracts.title: Normalize RC step defaults through measured-result generation
contracts.contract: Deck generation and metric-condition construction consume one validated normalized parameter object. Persist effective step voltage without rewriting input scope or retroactively changing historical identities. Omitted step_v and explicit 1.0 produce equivalent metrics/condition text, while candidate identities may differ because scopes differ.
verification: Native ngspice control with bounded measurements and omitted step_v completes checks; measured value agrees with analytic V*(1-exp(-t/RC)) within declared numerical tolerance.
Explicit and omitted defaults produce matching conditions; nondefault amplitude scales measured response.
Zero, negative, nonfinite and nonnumeric amplitudes remain unsupported; a failed simulator cannot produce a passing metric.
contracts.migration: No new baseline semantics; runtime policy identity changes and historical results remain historical. Do not silently rewrite scopes.
contracts.failure: Propagate execution errors as incomplete, never missing-data pass.

contracts.title: Make copper-width coverage explicit and include native arcs
contracts.contract: New versioned geometry criterion declares covered primitive classes and excludes nets explicitly. Width evidence lists primitive UUID/type/net/layer/value/limit plus eligible, checked, excluded and unsupported counts. Include native PCB_ARC with straight copper tracks. Via drill/annular ring and zone geometry are separate future criteria, not coerced into width.
verification: Actual KiCad fixture containing a 0.05 mm arc and five legal straight segments fails declared 0.20 mm broader copper-width criterion; straight-only legacy result retains its narrower meaning.
Arc-only valid and invalid boards, empty eligible set, excluded-net arcs, malformed primitive and unsupported copper class exercise coverage outcomes.
Evidence tampering or wrong candidate binding fails historical verification; no accepted defect from unsupported geometry.
contracts.migration: Opt-in new criterion/version; old scope/2 check definitions retain explicit straight-segment semantics. Require a new baseline to broaden existing campaign acceptance coverage.
contracts.failure: Empty or unknown eligible geometry produces incomplete coverage. Deterministic proven below-width primitive yields defect.

contracts.title: Audit executable acceptance coverage before launching reviews
contracts.contract: Versioned requirement intent distinguishes acceptance from informational obligations. A parameter-aware registry exposes can_evaluate_bound, required prerequisites and unsupported reasons. Compile a captured coverage report mapping each acceptance requirement to at least one defect-capable check. Informational requirements/checks remain traceable but cannot satisfy an acceptance obligation. Unknown capability blocks new-policy launch.
verification: Baseline mapping a functional acceptance requirement solely to netlist export or unbounded geometry is refused before model calls.
Mixed informational and bounded acceptance requirements compile and map every check.

Built-in mutation corpus demonstrates legal/wrong RC values, width violation and rule-check defects change expected criteria; unsupported/malformed mutants are not counted as detected physical defects.
Missing limits, unresolved prerequisites, unknown registry kind and informational-only baseline exercise refusals.

Run the full pipeline with scripted independent reviewer/adjudicator fixtures on deliberately broken reference boards and matched controls. Seal expected requirement violations separately from implementation outputs. Distinguish this harness test from live-model defect detection performance.
contracts.migration: New scope/baseline contract; do not reinterpret historical scope/2 results as audited. Explicit conversion preserves all acceptance requirements; no arbitrary waiver field.
contracts.failure: Capability is necessary coverage evidence, not semantic proof of requirement completeness. No model inference sets capability.

contracts.title: Reject empirical correction outside its declared design applicability
contracts.contract: Versioned calibration bundle binds each correction to source observation identity, baseline/check/metric/unit/condition, immutable model dependencies and a design applicability predicate. Initial predicate is exact captured design-dependency hashes; include all design inputs by default. Evidence producer/parser/model versions and calibration provenance remain captured. Mismatch prevents calibrated acceptance, records the failed predicate and requests new bench evidence. Qualified transfer envelopes are a later explicit policy, never inferred from topology similarity.
verification: Unchanged measured design replays its discrepancy interval against unchanged bounds.
Change a component value, connectivity, PCB geometry or unclassified design dependency: calibration becomes unavailable rather than silently transferring or producing a fabricated defect.
Changed model, metric/unit/condition, omitted observation, tampered raw sample and wrong baseline fail closed.
Re-ingest new candidate observations produces a new epoch; old acceptance remains superseded and old evidence retained.
contracts.migration: Legacy bundles stay verifiable under historical policy but do not acquire qualification. New strict campaigns require upgraded applicability; report migration need rather than silently widening predicates.
contracts.failure: Use missing-evidence/incomplete classification and structured recalibration request. No automatic widening, inverse model fit or claim that metadata authenticates instruments.

contracts.title: Explain incomplete campaigns without changing their state
contracts.contract: A diagnostic command produces a versioned machine report and readable evidence timeline. Include campaign/run/baseline identities, verified facts, failed invariants, unavailable facts, ambiguous transition candidates and operator actions with preconditions. Share pure verifier semantics; do not hide verifier exceptions. Read under an existing coherent lease or explicitly report unverified snapshot. Do not create lock files solely to diagnose historical data. Do not use F_GETLK as evidence about flock ownership without demonstrated platform-specific interoperability. Default diagnostic is advisory/unverified unless coherent reads are actually established. A .tmp file alone may reflect an active writer, not necessarily an interrupted write.
verification: Inject interruption at capture/check/review/adjudication/empirical boundaries and show only facts justified by retained artifacts.
Differential results match ordinary integrity verification on tampered and intact runs.
Byte/hash directory inventory before/after diagnosis is identical, including failure paths.
Concurrent writer yields an explicit busy/unverified result; partial .tmp files do not imply a uniquely known phase or safe retry.
contracts.migration: Additive output contract, no mutation or automatic recovery. Existing unreadable histories produce partial diagnostic with reasons.
contracts.failure: Unknown is an allowed result; offer zero/multiple actions when no single safe action is established. Pure verifier extraction can drift: read-only does not mean zero trust-kernel risk.

contracts.title: Enforce declared hardware interfaces across candidate repairs
contracts.contract: Owner-authored immutable interface specification enumerates required terminal identities, pin-to-net relations, required component/testpoint presence and allowed edits. A deterministic check maps those declarations onto each native candidate and emits bound violations. Reference identities derive from requirements, not prefix heuristics or a possibly defective first board. Distinguish named/anonymous nets and make renames explicit.
verification: Deletion of required load/testpoint, swapped external pins and disconnection each fail their declared invariant.
A legitimate resistor-value repair preserves interface checks and passes functional measurements.
R/C/L are not treated as transparent shorts; frequency-dependent networks do not become falsely equivalent.
Unknown symbol mapping and ambiguous terminal identities yield incomplete coverage; undeclared topology is not silently claimed protected.
contracts.migration: New check and captured contract require new baseline; no inferred obligations imposed retroactively. Public contract documents limits of graph equivalence.
contracts.failure: No changes to source candidate, scope or owner declarations by implementation agent. Unsupported mappings cannot become pass.

contracts.title: Turn unresolved concerns into reproducible evidence requests
contracts.contract: Versioned request binds candidate/baseline/requirement/concern, operating condition, requested observable and existing declared check if available. Coordinator may schedule already authorized deterministic verification. Reviewer experiments run only in isolated networkless sandbox, with bounded time/resources and retained script/tool/input/output hashes. Receipt reports execution and assertions separately; arbitrary exit code is never acceptance authority. New test proposals export a graduation bundle for a new explicitly authorized baseline/campaign.
verification: Concern tied to existing declared failed bound becomes accepted only through normal sealed coordinator-check witness validation.
Script reading candidate then exiting 1 cannot manufacture a defect; script success cannot resolve concern automatically.
Timeout, malformed output, missing interpreter, attempted network/write escape and changed candidate produce retained failed/unsupported receipts.
New check proposal leaves current baseline byte-identical and every initial reviewer context isolated.
contracts.migration: Additive concern/request/receipt schemas; current disposition vocabulary and acceptance rules remain authoritative. Human-readable actionable request even when no adapter supports it.
contracts.failure: Failed replay leaves concern unresolved. No automatic new thresholds, checks or requirement edits.

contracts.title: Ship a qualified passive tolerance-corner adapter
contracts.contract: Captured adapter specification declares supported passive topology, component tolerances, excitation/measurement conditions, finite corner grid, tool/model versions and qualification fixtures. Enumerate corners deterministically, retain each result and aggregate only the declared envelope. Initial analytically tractable RC response provides an independent oracle; expanded RLC support requires separate demonstrated bounds. Qualification must establish when endpoint extrema suffice; otherwise label sampled coverage rather than worst-case guarantee.
verification: Nominally passing RC fixture violates declared response at a tolerance corner and receives an evidence-backed defect.
Zero-tolerance result agrees with nominal analysis; independent analytic solution bounds each simulated corner within documented numerical error.
Unsupported topology/nonlinear parts, missing tolerance, excessive corner count and failed corner simulation yield incomplete coverage.
Model/tool/parser version change invalidates qualification; outputs preserve condition and unit identity for coupled metrics and empirical checks.
contracts.migration: New optional captured adapter/qualification contract and baseline criteria. No qualification conferred on arbitrary third-party solvers by hashing alone.
contracts.failure: Bounded resource budget; partial ensemble cannot masquerade as complete. Physical validation remains separate.

contracts.title: Recover interrupted bench-feedback transactions safely
contracts.contract: Versioned journal records operation identity from source candidate/report hash, target paths and intended review configuration. Explicit prepared, supersession_committed, review_started and completed states have durable receipts and directory fsync ordering. Under one writer lease, recovery validates identities/artifacts and reconciles only known deterministic transition steps. Same operation retries idempotently; changed report under same identity conflicts. A new model review remains a new identified attempt, never replayed automatically after uncertain external execution.
verification: Crash injection before/after each durable write and rename produces a recoverable state or explicit ambiguity without stale accepted outcome.
Two processes contend for same target: only one commits supersession/review start.
Duplicate operation produces one feedback event; conflicting identities refuse without clobbering files.
Uncertain provider execution is reported for operator resolution, not rerun; no instrument acquisition replay.
Recovered history verifies with retained original candidate and empirical receipts.
contracts.migration: Opt-in journal version for new operations. Legacy partial directories remain read-only diagnostic inputs unless explicit conversion proves their state; no guessed migration.
contracts.failure: Recovery scope ends at empirical ingestion and review launch. Preserve current convergence budget/epoch rules and all superseded evidence.

contracts.title: Index reviewer packets by entities and requirement coverage
contracts.contract: Deterministic packet index maps native component/pin/net/primitive IDs to requirements, checks, retained artifacts and declared coupling criteria. Full baseline and captured evidence remain programmatically reachable; index entries contain factual references, not prior reviewer opinions or inferred acceptance. Show missing/unmapped entities explicitly. Bounded display truncation includes continuation locators and coverage counts.
verification: Stable candidate produces stable index; entity rename and candidate change invalidate stale references.
Cross-domain check remains visible from both implicated entities with condition identity intact.
Fresh reviewer packets contain no peer judgments or campaign reviewer history.
Measured comparison on recorded fixtures reports token/latency and missed-defect outcomes; no savings claim without measurements.
Large/ambiguous netlists preserve full artifact access and mark partial index coverage.
contracts.migration: Additive versioned packet index; existing reviewers can ignore it. No narrowing of baseline/evidence permissions.
contracts.failure: Index failures cannot erase underlying evidence or grant pass; expose unavailable navigation.

contracts.title: Qualify PCB DC-resistance back-annotation for declared paths
contracts.contract: Captured stackup, copper thickness/resistivity/reference temperature, operating temperature and terminal mapping drive deterministic resistance extraction for an explicitly supported trace/via network. Native straight and arc lengths/widths become resistor-network edges. Solve declared DC load cases and emit voltage-drop/loss metrics through existing measurement/coupling contracts. Unsupported zones or ambiguous connections refuse until a qualified model exists. Initial scope is DC conduction, not switching parasitics or thermal fields.
verification: Straight and arc paths agree with rho*L/A; series/parallel supported networks agree with independent analytic resistance solutions.
Actual KiCad fixture with narrowed/lengthened trace produces expected voltage-drop failure under declared current.
Missing stackup, temperature, unresolved terminal, unsupported zone and disconnected path yield incomplete coverage.
Model inputs, extracted network and solver outputs are captured and tamper checked; nominal/worst dimensional cases are distinguished.
Any added via or parallel-path support has its own oracle and qualification before inclusion.
contracts.migration: Optional new adapter and explicit baseline requirements. No retroactive claim of RLC extraction or EMC/DFM certification.
contracts.failure: Do not infer board materials or fabrication tolerances from defaults. Refuse outside qualified geometry and temperature domain.

contracts.title: Refuse environment drift before spending review inference
contracts.contract: Before each reviewer, adjudicator and implementation call, compare declared tool/runtime/policy identities to captured execution expectations and emit a retained preflight receipt. Validate required binaries and sandbox availability without invoking a model. Optional qualified native canary uses declared numerical tolerances and supported version ranges; no bit-identical numerical promise. Refusal consumes no inference call and cannot adjudicate or repair a candidate.
verification: Replace a captured binary or policy between check completion and reviewer launch: call hook records zero provider invocations and explicit incomplete drift result.
Unchanged supported environment launches normal independent calls; no prior review content enters other reviewer contexts.
Missing binary, broken sandbox and malformed receipt refuse with specific diagnostic; canary failure is execution coverage failure, not design defect.
Check drift separately at implementation and adjudication boundaries; report that preflight does not eliminate races with later external upgrades or establish subscription quota.
contracts.migration: Additive versioned receipt for new executions; preserve old evidence policy identities. No new acceptance criterion or automatic repair lane.
contracts.failure: No one-token model quota canary or automatic provider fallback. Known authentication/quota failure stops affected operation under existing routing rules.
